ic10/catalog-control-plane/catalog_coord.note: Five on-demand control-plane tools post commands at S21/S22, the migration pair also at S40..S42. An operator runs one of them at a time against a claimed Coordinator and none is resident, so nothing posts while another tool waits.

The freeze/ack cell S16 is driven by whichever publisher the adapter is wired to: a Bridge feeding a Snapshot Host, or a Registry Host directly. One adapter has one publisher; the two are alternative directory topologies, never both on one adapter.

ic10/controller-config/generic_persisten.note: A Config Host pairs with exactly one Config Policy, which is what gives its records a meaning. The six policies are the alternative meanings a host can be given; a deployment wires one per host instance and a second policy on the same host is a wiring error, not a race.

ic10/controller-discovery/controller_dir.note: The freeze/ack cell S16 is driven by whichever publisher the adapter is wired to: a Bridge feeding a Snapshot Host, or a Registry Host directly. One adapter has one publisher; the two are alternative directory topologies, never both on one adapter.

ic10/dependency-planning/dependency_chil.note: All three post from inside the Planner's call tree and each waits for its response before returning, and the Planner serves one Gate or cleanup request at a time. The stock-target Future View reaches Child Validity only through its own dedicated Claim View, which brings a dedicated Child Validity and Job Monitor with it (see dependency_claim_view).

ic10/dependency-planning/dependency_clai.note: Plan Builder and Release Advisor post under the Planner. The Future View posts once per active matching job from an independent loop; on one shared instance its next request lands before the callee latches the Planner-side request and strands it (tests/test_mailbox_arbitration.py). The stock-target deployment therefore runs its own Claim View, and with it its own Child Validity and Job Monitor.

ic10/dependency-planning/dependency_plan.note: The Existing controller looks a plan up while the Planner waits on it; upsert and clear are the Planner's own requests. One call tree, one request at a time.

ic10/dependency-planning/generic_job_mon.note: The Cancellation Guard scans plan records on its own loop and monitors each parent it finds; the Planner's tree monitors children while a plan is built or evaluated. Neither waits on the other, so the Guard is wired to a Job Monitor of its own. The Monitor only reads the Job Store, so both instances share it.

ic10/dependency-planning/item_producer_r.note: Child Creator posts under the Planner; Producer View posts under the stock-target Evaluator. The resolver is a generated table with no downstream mailbox, so the second instance is one housing.

ic10/dependency-planning/job_inventory_p.note: The Existing controller's evaluator and the New controller both post under the Planner, which runs one of them per request and waits on it.

ic10/dependency-planning/job_requirement.note: Three planning clients post under the Planner. Producer View posts under the stock-target Evaluator, and the stock-target Child Validity posts to that same dedicated instance under the same root. A Requirement View instance brings its Reagent Resolver with it; the two profile views it selects are re-validated snapshots (reselect) and stay shared.

ic10/generic-jobs/generic_job_selector_v.note: Each scheduler boots its selector into its own mode (S18 = 0 manufacturing, 4 exact JobType.POWER) and owns the cursor at S19/S20; the two domains deploy separate selector instances over the one Job Store, which the selector only reads.

ic10/item-storage-common/item_resource_r.note: Preflight quotes under the Planner; Inventory View quotes under the stock-target Evaluator. The Selector only reads its Snapshot Host and the endpoints it quotes, so a second instance shares those. The Allocator never posts: it reads a quote fenced on the response token it was handed and re-checks that token after reading.

ic10/manufacturing-ingress/stock_target_.note: The Evaluator posts its evaluation request, then hands the target to the Ingress and waits on it; the Ingress posts the mutation-time request while the Evaluator waits. One root, blocking at every hop. The Evaluator starts no evaluation while the Ingress holds an unanswered request (S25 != S26), so an Evaluator reflashed mid-request waits for the Ingress instead of posting beside it.

ic10/manufacturing/manufacturing_candida.note: docs/MANUFACTURING_SCHEDULER.md deploys one dynamic selector for both domains because the manufacturing control plane is serial: the Scheduler drives one driver at a time through the Driver Router and each driver posts one selection request and waits on it.

ic10/manufacturing/transform_lane_direct.note: The freeze/ack cell S16 is driven by whichever publisher the adapter is wired to: a Bridge feeding a Snapshot Host, or a Registry Host directly. One adapter has one publisher; the two are alternative directory topologies, never both on one adapter.

ic10/material-transform/multi_material_r.note: Transform lanes keep their own Resolver/Stager/Allocator instances and printing runs a separate print reservation lane over the same protocol; the mutable reservation instances are never multiplexed across domains (docs/MANUFACTURING_SCHEDULER.md).

ic10/power-grid/power_dispatch_plan_stor.note: The Cycle owns the BEGIN/COMMIT boundaries and waits on the Sweep, which waits on each Flow Builder; one dispatch transaction at a time.

ic10/power-grid/power_reservation_direct.note: The freeze/ack cell S16 is driven by whichever publisher the adapter is wired to: a Bridge feeding a Snapshot Host, or a Registry Host directly. One adapter has one publisher; the two are alternative directory topologies, never both on one adapter.

ic10/power-jobs/power_job_lifecycle_clie.note: The POWER Scheduler drives Prepare and Finalize one step at a time through register-indexed port dr9, resolved to its d1 and d2 by the reviewed register_ports override, and waits on each step's response before selecting the next job.

ic10/power-jobs/power_policy_target_reso.note: Prepare and Finalize run one step at a time under the POWER Scheduler through register-indexed port dr9 (its d1 and d2), and Policy Apply posts while Prepare waits on it.

ic10/pressure-grid/pressure_grid_link_di.note: The freeze/ack cell S16 is driven by whichever publisher the adapter is wired to: a Bridge feeding a Snapshot Host, or a Registry Host directly. One adapter has one publisher; the two are alternative directory topologies, never both on one adapter.

ic10/pressure-grid/pressure_reservation_.note: Both post under the Reservation Planner's plan build, which waits on each; one plan at a time.

ic10/printer-directory/printer_execution.note: The freeze/ack cell S16 is driven by whichever publisher the adapter is wired to: a Bridge feeding a Snapshot Host, or a Registry Host directly. One adapter has one publisher; the two are alternative directory topologies, never both on one adapter.

ic10/recipe-catalog/recipe_execution_pro.note: A selected snapshot, not a token mailbox: each consumer writes the RecipeHash to S10 and reads nothing until S49 echoes it. The Print Job Driver and the Operator Recipe View read the rest in the same slice as that check; the Requirement View's reads can span a tick, so it also requires S14 unchanged afterwards. A competing selection costs a retry, never a wrong read. Operator orders deploy a dedicated instance regardless (docs/OPERATOR_ORDER_INGRESS.md).

ic10/transform-catalog/resource_transfor.note: One writer program today; declared so that a dedicated Requirement View instance does not drag a profile view with it. The Requirement View selects S70 and re-checks the S68 echo, S69 status, and S74 generation after reading, so two instances selecting at once cost each other a retry.
